data.name: Eve
data.message: Heading to weapons then back through electrical

I found Bob's body in security. Here's my route: I started in navigation, moved to security where I saw both Bob and Charlie at tick 6 — Charlie had just entered security from electrical. I then went to weapons to do a task, and when I came back to security, Bob was dead on the floor.

Charlie was the last person I saw with Bob in security. That's very suspicious to me. I'd like to hear Charlie explain where they went after I left for weapons.

I came from cafeteria -> medbay -> electrical, then into security. I did see Bob there, and Eve was there too. Eve left toward weapons pretty much right after that, and I left security down to navigation — I was not sitting in security with Bob after she left.

I’m in navigation now, and I never went back up to security. So from my point of view, the only people I saw around Bob were Eve and Bob. Eve is reporting it, which is fine, but she also admits she left and then came back. The kill could’ve happened after I left, and she’s pinning “last seen” on me because I passed through.

I’d like to know if anyone saw Eve actually in weapons doing the task, because I can only confirm she went that direction.

My route was storage → lower engine → storage → medbay. I was doing tasks the whole time and unfortunately didn't see anyone — no one passed through with me, and I can't vouch for or against anyone directly.

So I have to go on what Eve and Charlie are saying. Both of them place themselves in security with Bob, and their stories actually line up with each other on that point — Eve left for weapons, Charlie left for navigation. The question is who's lying about leaving.

A couple of things I'd want to know: Did anyone see Charlie arrive in navigation around that time? That would clear him. And did anyone see Eve actually in weapons? Whoever can be confirmed by a third party is the cleaner one. Frank and Alice haven't spoken yet — their info is going to be critical here. I'm not ready to vote either Eve or Charlie without more confirmation. Frank, Alice, please tell us if you saw either of them where they claim to have been.

My route was lower engine → storage → medbay → electrical, doing tasks the whole way. Unfortunately, I didn't see a single other player the entire round — no one in storage, no one in medbay, and I'm in electrical now alone.

That's actually a little interesting because Charlie claims he went cafeteria → medbay → electrical → security. If Charlie was in medbay and electrical before me, our paths should have been close in timing, but I can't confirm or deny seeing him — we may have just missed each other.

More importantly, I can't confirm Eve in weapons OR Charlie in navigation. So I can't clear either of them directly.

What I can say is this: Eve's story has a structural issue. She admits she left Bob alive with Charlie, went to weapons, then came back and found him dead. That's a self-report after being alone — classic setup. Charlie's story is consistent and he placed himself moving away from security toward navigation, which matches where he is now on the map.

I'm leaning slightly toward Eve being suspicious, but I want to hear Frank before committing. Frank, if you were anywhere near weapons or security, your info decides this.

My route was upper engine → oxygen → upper engine → lower engine, doing tasks the whole way. I didn't see anyone — I was on the west side of the map the entire round, nowhere near security or weapons.

So I can't directly confirm or deny Eve in weapons or Charlie in navigation. That's frustrating because, like Alice said, my info would have been decisive.

Let me work with what we have. Diana was storage → lower engine → storage → medbay. Alice was lower engine → storage → medbay → electrical. Their paths overlap heavily — they should have seen each other, but neither did. That's a little odd, but it can happen with timing.

On Eve vs Charlie: Eve self-reports after being alone in weapons, which is the classic suspicious pattern Alice pointed out. But Charlie's story also has him in security with Bob right before the kill. The key detail for me is that Eve volunteered "Charlie was the last person I saw with Bob" — which is exactly what a duck would say to redirect after killing.

Also, Charlie being in navigation now is at least consistent with his claimed route. Eve being the reporter means she came back to security — which she'd have to do whether innocent or guilty.

I'm leaning Eve. Her story requires us to trust that she went to weapons and came back, with no witnesses, and she's the one pushing hardest on Charlie. I'll vote Eve.

Wait, I need to clarify — I already spoke first, and now the discussion has come back to me with everyone else having weighed in. Let me respond to what's been said.

Frank, I hear you, but your reasoning is shaky. Yes, I self-reported — but someone had to find Bob, and I'm being honest about my exact movements. If I were the killer, why would I volunteer that I was alone with Bob and Charlie right before? I'd make up a witness or claim I was elsewhere.

Here's what bothers me about Charlie's story: he says he went cafeteria → medbay → electrical → security → navigation. Alice was on the path medbay → electrical and saw NO ONE. If Charlie really went through medbay and electrical, Alice should have crossed him. Their timing is close enough that a complete miss is suspicious.

Also, Charlie conveniently "passed through" security right when Bob died, then immediately left to a far corner of the map where no one could verify him. That's the cleaner setup, not mine.

I'm not going to vote myself. I'm voting Charlie. He had means, opportunity, and his route conflicts with Alice's observations.

Eve, that doesn’t clear you — reporters can absolutely give accurate routes when the route itself is the cover.

The timing issue with Alice doesn’t prove anything. I moved cafeteria → medbay → electrical before reaching security, and Alice says she was moving lower engine → storage → medbay → electrical. Those are opposite directions and could easily miss by a few ticks, especially if one of us was already in/out of a room. Alice even said she can’t confirm or deny me.

What we do know is:

- Bob was alive in security when I saw him.
- Eve was also there.
- Eve left toward weapons.
- I left down to navigation and never came back.
- Eve is the one who returned to security and reported the body.
- Nobody can confirm Eve actually did weapons.

Eve keeps framing “Charlie was last seen with Bob,” but from my perspective Eve had just as much opportunity, and she’s the one who came back to the body and is now pushing the person who can contradict her.

I’m still voting Eve here.

I've already spoken once, but since the discussion has come back around, let me weigh in on where we've landed.

The case really is Eve vs. Charlie, and the rest of us — me, Alice, Frank — have no direct visual on either of them at their claimed alibis. So we have to reason from structure.

Eve's point about Alice and Charlie's paths is weaker than she's making it sound. Alice went lower engine → storage → medbay → electrical. Charlie went cafeteria → medbay → electrical → security. They cross at medbay and electrical, but in opposite directions — it's very plausible to miss by a tick or two. Alice herself said "we may have just missed each other." That's not a contradiction, that's normal.

What's harder to explain away is the self-report pattern. Eve was the last person confirmed near Bob, left to a room no one can verify her in, came back, and found the body. Classic setup. And her pivot to "I'm voting Charlie" only after Frank named her feels reactive, not principled.

Charlie's location now — navigation — is at least consistent with his stated route. Eve's weapons trip is unverifiable and conveniently isolates her.

I'm going with Frank and Charlie on this. I'll vote Eve. If I'm wrong, I'll own it, but the structural evidence points her way.

I'll keep this short since I already spoke and the room has largely converged.

To recap my position: my route was lower engine → storage → medbay → electrical, all task work, no encounters. I couldn't confirm Charlie through medbay/electrical, but as Diana correctly pointed out, opposite-direction paths can easily miss by a tick or two — that's not a contradiction, just normal timing.

What's tipped me firmly toward Eve:

1. The self-report pattern — alone with Bob and Charlie, leaves to an unverifiable room, comes back, finds body. Textbook.
2. Eve's pivot. She opened by asking Charlie to explain himself, calmly. Then the moment Frank named her, she suddenly "discovered" a contradiction between my route and Charlie's that she didn't mention in her first speech. If that timing issue were real, she'd have raised it immediately. It's reactive.
3. Charlie's current location matches his claimed route. Eve's doesn't get verified by anyone.

I'm voting Eve.

I'll keep this brief since the room has converged and I already laid out my reasoning earlier.

Nothing has changed my read. Eve's structural pattern is the classic self-report setup: alone with the victim, leaves to an unverifiable room, comes back, finds the body. And as Alice sharply pointed out, Eve's "contradiction" about Alice and Charlie's paths only surfaced after she was named — if it were a real catch, she'd have led with it in her first speech. That reactive pivot is damning.

Charlie's location in navigation is at least consistent with his claimed route. Eve's weapons trip is verified by no one.

I'm sticking with my vote: Eve.

data.message: All my tasks are done. Want to buddy up? Safer together with so few of us left.

I found Alice's body in cafeteria when I just arrived there. My route was lower engine, storage, medbay, electrical, security, weapons, security, navigation, security, weapons, then cafeteria where I found her.

Key info: I saw Alice alive at tick 24 in weapons, then she left to cafeteria at tick 25. I was doing tasks elsewhere after that. Diana was in navigation ticks 34-36 — I saw her there clearly.

With Eve already ejected (and she was wrong, since people kept dying), and Bob and Alice both dead, that leaves me, Charlie, and Diana alive. I can vouch I was nowhere near cafeteria until just now. Diana was in navigation when I saw her, but I lost sight of her after tick 36 — she had time to get to cafeteria.

Charlie — I haven't seen you all round. Where were you? That's my main question. Between you and Diana, one of you killed Alice.

I was mostly on the left/middle side late round. My route was weapons/cafeteria early, then oxygen → upper engine → medbay/electrical area, then security/weapons a bit, and near the end I went cafeteria → medbay → storage → lower engine. I’m in lower engine now, nowhere near cafeteria when the report happened.

I did see Alice alive in cafeteria around tick 37 while I was passing through, but I didn’t see Diana at all. If Frank saw Diana in navigation at 34-36, she absolutely had time to go navigation → security → weapons → cafeteria after that. I don’t think this is Frank self-reporting with that detailed route and timing — Diana is the one whose gap fits best to me.

Let me lay out exactly what I saw, because Frank's story has a serious problem.

My route: upper engine → medbay → electrical → security → weapons → security → navigation. I stayed in navigation doing the chart task from tick ~33 onward until this meeting.

Here's the key: Frank says he saw me in navigation ticks 34-36. That's true — because HE was in navigation with me! I saw Frank enter navigation from security at tick 29, and he stayed there until tick 36 when he left toward security. So Frank wasn't doing some long task route ending at cafeteria — he was sitting in navigation with me, then left at tick 36 heading back through security toward... cafeteria.

Also, Frank claims his route was "lower engine, storage, medbay, electrical, security, weapons, security, navigation, security, weapons, then cafeteria." But I saw Frank enter electrical from MEDBAY at tick 16, and enter security from WEAPONS at tick 26 — that matches. Then navigation at 29-36, then he left toward security/weapons/cafeteria. He had the perfect window to kill Alice in cafeteria after leaving me at tick 36.

Charlie, meanwhile, says he saw Alice alive in cafeteria around tick 37 — but Frank left navigation at 36 heading that direction. Frank is the self-reporter here. He's trying to pin it on me because I'm his alibi witness — but the alibi cuts both ways, and his post-tick-36 movement puts him at the body.

I'm voting Frank.

Wait, I'm speaker 1? My speech is already up there as Frank's. Let me address Diana's accusation directly since I have more to say.

Diana, that's a lie. I was NOT in navigation from tick 29-36. My route had me at security/weapons during those early ticks. I only arrived at navigation at tick 34, saw you there at 34, 35, 36, then I left back through security toward weapons and then cafeteria where I found Alice's body.

If I had killed Alice, why would I report? I could have walked away. The body was right there in cafeteria — anyone passing through would find it.

Diana is fabricating a timeline to flip the script. She claims I was "sitting in navigation" the whole time — but Charlie just said he passed through cafeteria around tick 37 and saw Alice ALIVE. If Diana was locked in navigation doing chart task from tick 33 onward, fine — but I left navigation at 36, went security → weapons (that's 4 ticks of travel), arriving cafeteria around tick 40+. Alice was killed AFTER Charlie saw her at 37, and Diana had the shortest path: navigation → security → cafeteria is doable.

I'm voting Diana. Charlie, you're the swing — think about who actually had the cleaner window.

The key point for me is Alice was alive in cafeteria around tick 37 when I passed through. I left after that toward medbay/storage/lower engine, so the kill had to be after 37.

Diana, your story is basically “I stayed in navigation,” but the only person who can confirm that is Frank, and he says he left at 36. From navigation, either of you could physically reach cafeteria after 37, but Frank is the one who reported instead of just leaving the body for someone else. With only three of us alive, self-reporting there feels riskier than just walking away if he killed.

Also your accusation shifted hard onto Frank only after he named you as the suspect, and you’re using the fact he saw you in navigation as a weapon against him. I don’t have a hard clear on either of you, but based on the timing, I trust Frank’s version more.

I’m voting Diana.

I need to be direct here because Charlie is being swayed by Frank's framing.

Frank just lied in his last speech. He said "I was NOT in navigation from tick 29-36... I only arrived at navigation at tick 34." But I have clear observations: Frank entered navigation from security at tick 29, and I saw him there at ticks 33, 34, and 35. He left at tick 36 heading back to security. That's 7 ticks in navigation with me — not a quick pass-through at 34.

Why does this matter? Because Frank's original speech claimed a long task route: "security, weapons, security, navigation, security, weapons, then cafeteria." He's padding his route to make it look like he was busy doing tasks far from cafeteria. In reality, he sat in navigation with me, then went navigation → security → cafeteria after tick 36. That's a 4-tick trip, putting him in cafeteria around tick 40 — perfectly matching killing Alice after Charlie saw her alive at 37.

Charlie, think carefully: Frank's route as stated doesn't match what I witnessed. He's lying about his timeline RIGHT NOW in this meeting. Self-reporting isn't suspicious when the body is in a high-traffic room like cafeteria and he knows someone else will find it soon — reporting first lets him control the narrative, which is exactly what he's doing.

I was doing the chart task in navigation the whole time after Frank left. I had no kill opportunity. Frank did.

Voting Frank.
